notes: Access: curl_cffi impersonate=chrome131, ~5-8s pacing; all 12 pages fetched (200) after the homepage's own 429/px-captcha (homepage-only, not encountered on any deep link). Discovery: SSR mega-nav JSON contains a BlockBuilderCuratedNavigationGroup whose children are 10 department-scoped 'New in X' curated pages plus a roll-up link labelled 'All New Arrivals' -> https://www.jossandmain.com/curated/new-arrivals~ev569309.html. Opened the parent: genuine PLP, visible '585 Items' header, browseResultCount=585, totalSKUCount=585, eventRoadsign 'New Arrivals Are Here', real BrowseGrid with pagination (hasNextPage:true). Opened each of the 10 department children and recorded their own resultCount the same way: Living Room 51, Bedroom 48, Kitchen & Dining 65, Outdoor 22, Office 5, Rugs 32, Lighting 30, Bedding 11, Decor 261, Reno 60 -- these sum to exactly 585, matching the parent's own count exactly, confirming 'All New Arrivals' is an exact roll-up of these 10 children (same exact-roll-up pattern this company's prior Home-Decor pass documented, e.g. Decorative Objects cat = its own sb0 children summed exactly). Per this brief's own worked example ('New Arrivals > Furniture New Arrivals / Lighting New Arrivals'), kept the parent as a grouping row plus all 10 children as leaves rather than dropping the parent, since the parent is itself an independently valid, browsable PLP (not a pure navigational label). 'New in Reno' was inspected specifically since 'Reno' is ambiguous out of context -- its own eventRoadsign is literally 'New in Reno' and its products are ordinary newly-added home-renovation-adjacent goods, not an unrelated campaign, so it was kept as a genuine department leaf. Checked seo-category-sitemap~0.xml (166 URLs) and all 3 seo-keyword-sitemap shards (~104k URLs) for new-arrival/new-in slugs -- zero matches; these curated pages are nav-only, not separately SEO-indexed. Joss & Main is Wayfair-family (Next.js/BlockBuilderBrowse, browsePageType:3 curated-event pages, same /curated/<slug>~ev<id>.html URL family used for its Best Sellers and Clearance/Closeout listings in this same batch) -- AllModern/Birch Lane (also in this batch, same platform) likely expose an analogous department-split New Arrivals nav group worth checking for the same roll-up pattern.
